head.citation-title: Flexural behavior of circular PHC piles strengthened with steel sleeve grouting
head.abstracts: © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.High-pile wharves are prone to damage under the action of complex marine environments. The steel sleeve grouting reinforcement technology is used to repair damaged PHC piles. This paper researches the flexural performance of circular PHC piles strengthened with steel sleeve grouting (CPSG). The tests illustrate the failure process and mode of CPSG under bending loads. ABAQUS-based finite element models were constructed, and their reliability was confirmed through comparison between simulation results and experimental data. On this basis, a sensitivity analysis was conducted. The numerical simulation results show that increasing steel sleeve thickness (t), steel sleeve yield strength (fy), and grouting material thickness (δ) can improve flexural bearing capacity and stiffness, while increasing grouting material strength (fc) has little effect on the flexural bearing capacity, but it can improve the stiffness to a certain extent, and pre-stressed reinforcement diameter (d) has little impact on the flexural bearing capacity and stiffness. Finally, the force and moment equilibrium equations were established based on the verified plane section assumption, and thus the formula for the ultimate flexural bearing capacity of CPSG was derived. The favorable agreement among theory, simulation, and experiment validates the comprehensive approach and provides reliable guidance for engineering applications of CPSG.

coredata.dc:description: High-pile wharves are prone to damage under the action of complex marine environments. The steel sleeve grouting reinforcement technology is used to repair damaged PHC piles. This paper researches the flexural performance of circular PHC piles strengthened with steel sleeve grouting (CPSG). The tests illustrate the failure process and mode of CPSG under bending loads. ABAQUS-based finite element models were constructed, and their reliability was confirmed through comparison between simulation results and experimental data. On this basis, a sensitivity analysis was conducted. The numerical simulation results show that increasing steel sleeve thickness (t), steel sleeve yield strength (fy), and grouting material thickness (δ) can improve flexural bearing capacity and stiffness, while increasing grouting material strength (fc) has little effect on the flexural bearing capacity, but it can improve the stiffness to a certain extent, and pre-stressed reinforcement diameter (d) has little impact on the flexural bearing capacity and stiffness. Finally, the force and moment equilibrium equations were established based on the verified plane section assumption, and thus the formula for the ultimate flexural bearing capacity of CPSG was derived. The favorable agreement among theory, simulation, and experiment validates the comprehensive approach and provides reliable guidance for engineering applications of CPSG.
coredata.dc:title: Flexural behavior of circular PHC piles strengthened with steel sleeve grouting
